hints.title: Grouping by Date and Worker
hints.text: Group records by both the event date and the employee identification to aggregate daily duration.

hints.title: Computing Session Durations
hints.text: Calculate the duration of each shift by subtracting the check-in timestamp from the check-out timestamp.

hints.title: Summing Daily Durations
hints.text: Apply the sum aggregate function over the computed shift lengths and rename the date column to day.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT event_day AS day, emp_id, SUM(out_time - in_time) AS total_time
FROM Employees
GROUP BY event_day, emp_id;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) or O(N) with an index on (event_day, emp_id)
complexity.space: O(N) for grouped hash aggregation buckets
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Row-by-row iteration in application memory is inefficient compared to declarative database aggregation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Composite indexes on grouping attributes allow index-only stream aggregation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should aggregate total duration per employee per day and format column aliases accurately.
